description.narrative: Following a review on the progress of the implementation of IFMIS by a World Bank Supervision Mission from June 14th -18th, 2010, it was noted that some of thecritical but soft components of PFM reform actions, required to complement other interventions, were not being carried out. Capacity building was one major activity that was skewed to ICT-based systems when it would take several years before such capacity is even built across line Ministries and Agencies. In the short to medium term, it has been found necessary to implement other complementary ctions and at the same time establish an improved coordination mechanisms to ensure that reforms are better sequenced, coordinated and prioritized to achieve overall development outcomes. This requires institution strengthening within and beyond the Ministry of Finance # the focal point of PFM improvement supported under existing interventions. The EGIRP is one project that provides support in key PFM improvement areas but does not cover the specific institutional and operation capacity improvement areas proposed under this grant. Coordination with other development partners in PFM improvement, though fragmented and relatively weak, has been in place since the GEMAP and this grant will help strengthen this coordination mechanism, among others. As Liberia has also reached the HIPC completion point in June 2010, the necessity to further strengthen the PFM institutions, particularly in relation to M&As capacity to manage their budget execution processes, becomes even more acute. # # It is also noted that the newly established PFM Reform Secretariat in the Ministry of Finance is a step in the right direction, but the capacity of the Secretariat in coordinating reforms is uneven and would need strengthening. The Secretariat will serve as a catalytic entity that will coordinate the overall PFM reforms that are currently fragmented. Funding for supporting the ultimate sustenance of the Secretariat is a critical activity that the GoL desperately needs. The grant will support this activitiy that is closely aligned to PFM strengthening.
